# metal:TransmonConcentric

The base `TrasmonConcentric` class .

**Source:** Metal (Qiskit Metal). **Category:** qubit. **Module:** `qiskit_metal.qlibrary.qubits.transmon_concentric`.

See also the [catalog](../CATALOG.md) and the [duplicates decisions](../DUPLICATES.md).

## Pins

![Pins of metal:TransmonConcentric](../../images/components/metal_TransmonConcentric.png)

Pin image (default parameters). Light = metal, dark = etched gap, colours = junction layers. A red dot and arrow is a pin and its direction (out of the cell); the red bar is the CPW width a + 2 b. Blue dot = a pin without direction. Units: µm.

| pin | x (µm) | y (µm) | direction (°) | a (µm) | b (µm) | purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pin1` | -750 | 270 | 180 | 10 | 6 | LOM node `pin1` |
| `pin2` | 750 | -40 | 0 | 10 | 6 | control line (flux) in the LOM |
| `pin3` | 750 | 40 | 0 | 10 | 6 | control line (flux) in the LOM |
| `squid_a` | 0 | 115 | none | 10 | 6 | junction pins (the LOM's L_J); LOM node `island1` |
| `squid_b` | 0 | 150 | none | 10 | 6 | junction pins (the LOM's L_J); LOM node `island2` |

Pins with direction `none`: `squid_a`, `squid_b`. They mark a point (a junction lead, a pad centre), not a CPW end. The KLayout ghost draws them as boxes. A route can start there only where the notes say so; it cannot be snapped to.

a, b: CPW centre width and gap where the pin declares them (`–` = not declared). Position and direction are in the cell's own frame (`at=(0, 0)`, `rot=0`).

## Parameters

| name | default | unit | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `a` | `10` | μm | Width of center conductor |
| `b` | `6` | μm | Width of gap |
| `r` | `100` | μm | Turn radius |
| `junction_type` | `"Metal"` | – | Junction as fabricated: Metal footprint, or a trilayer cell placed on each junction line |
| `junction_params` | `"{}"` | – | Trilayer junction cell parameters (JSON dict, e.g. lj_nH) |
| `metal_class` | `"TransmonConcentric"` | – | Quantum Metal component |
| `options` | `"{}"` | – | Metal options as JSON (bare numbers on length options are µm) |
| `open_pins` | `""` | – | Pins left open (comma-separated): keep Metal's etch beyond them, as drawn with no route attached |

Electrically relevant parameters (sizes, gaps, junction, ports) come first, the rest follows.

## LOM model

The cell contributes to the lumped model:

| branch | type | nodes | value (estimate at defaults) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `C_X_1` | C | island1 – gnd | estimate=39, unit=fF, estimate_source=rough: ring, estimate_kind=rough, uncertainty=±50% |
| `C_X_2` | C | island2 – gnd | estimate=16, unit=fF, estimate_source=rough: disk to ground, screened by the ring, estimate_kind=rough, uncertainty=±50% |
| `C_X_12` | C | island1 – island2 | estimate=90, unit=fF, estimate_source=rough: disk–ring facing edges (CPS), estimate_kind=rough, uncertainty=±50% |
| `J_X` | SQUID | island1 – island2 | Lj_nH=–, Cj_fF=0, asym=0, flux_phi0=0 |
| `Cg_X_pin1` | C | island1 – pin1 | estimate=15, unit=fF, estimate_source=rough: readout line over the ring (CPS), estimate_kind=rough, uncertainty=±50% |
| `Cc_X_pin1` | C | pin1 – gnd | estimate=54, unit=fF, estimate_source=rough: readout line in the pocket (wide-gap CPW), estimate_kind=rough, uncertainty=±50% |

Nodes: `island1`, `island2`, `pin1`.

## How to use

In Python:

```python
from quantcore_circuits.designer import Designer

d = Designer("demo", box=(0, 0, 7500, 7500))
d.add("U1", "metal:TransmonConcentric", at=(3750, 3750), a=10)   # parameters: see the table above
d.add("PAD", "BondPad", at=(1125, 3750), rot=270)   # a launcher to connect to
d.route("L1", "PAD.a", "U1.pin1")                # a CPW from the pad to the pin
```

Pin names go into `d.route(...)` as `INSTANCE.pin`, and into `snap=` / `to=` when placing. From the shell: `qcc components metal:TransmonConcentric` lists the pins; add `--schema` for the parameters.

In KLayout: Quantcore panel ▸ Components ▸ double-click the cell, then click on the layout to place it. Rotate and mirror before the click; use Connect on two pins to route.
